baseline.note: NOT MOVED THIS CYCLE, deliberately. Cycle 5 DID run the model and DID measure the canonical prompt twice in one process: 16.96 and 17.04 tok/s spec (evidence/cycle5.log PT0/PT8), base AR 95.6 ms/tok = 10.46 tok/s. That is +0.8% on 16.86, which is inside the +/-1% cross-run band (invariant 6), and the only shipped-path changes it carried (a LARGER shared-memory request, two skipped no-op launches, one TLS read per dsync) cannot produce a speedup by construction. Adopting +0.8% here would be Finding 33 with a network attached. The comparable cycle-3 numbers are 16.83/16.90 spec and 96.8 ms/tok base, so the two runs agree to within noise and the baseline is CONFIRMED, not stale.

queue.what: the illegal memory access reported at kernels/indexer.cu:96 (was :91) is NOT a prefill-length defect. Finding 54: it followed SMAX when SMAX moved 18 -> 28 (cycle 3 died in prompt 2's prefill when p2 was longest; cycle 5 died in prompt 4's prefill once p4 was longest, while p2 prefilled 4x cleanly), BUT build/gate_prefill_len at the exact lengths 5,10,14,17,21,24,27 in both weight alignments PASSES with 0 errors, and in cycle 3 the SMAX prompt survived three prefills before faulting on the fourth. New frame: something ACCUMULATES across sweep points and the longest prompt is merely the first allocation big enough to fall off the end of it. Prime suspect: 8 raw cudaMalloc/cudaFree per indexer layer per call (kernels/indexer.cu:78-83 + kernels/compressed_attn.cu:62), 21 layers per prefill, inside a 122.8 GiB managed pool with 111.5 GiB of resident weights (~11 GiB headroom). Sizes are correct by inspection, so this is about allocator behaviour, not a wrong size.
queue.falsify: NO MODEL RUN NEEDED FIRST. (1) print cudaMemGetInfo free/total at every sweep-point boundary and around indexer_forward; (2) write a standalone gate that replays N cycles of the indexer's malloc/free pattern at ascending s inside a pool deliberately reduced to ~11 GiB free, and see whether free memory decays or an allocation fails. If free memory is FLAT across points, the accumulation frame is dead and the next suspect is arena_reset / the per-point head rebuild, not the allocator. Only after a unit-level answer should a model run be spent.
